questions.stem: Photosynthesis uses light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. Why is photosynthesis classified as endothermic?

options.text: Because it happens in living organisms
Because energy is continuously absorbed from light to drive the reaction
Because it produces oxygen gas
Because it happens slowly over time

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is endothermic because the products (glucose and oxygen) contain more chemical energy than the reactants (carbon dioxide and water). Light energy is absorbed and stored as chemical energy in glucose molecules. Without continuous light energy input, the reaction cannot proceed.

questions.stem: A student dissolves ammonium nitrate in water and the temperature drops from 20°C to 8°C. She uses 100 g of water (specific heat capacity = 4.2 J/g/°C). How much energy was absorbed by the dissolving process?
questions.explanation: Using Q = mcDeltaT: Q = 100 x 4.2 x (20 - 8) = 100 x 4.2 x 12 = 5040 J. The temperature dropped by 12°C, meaning 5040 J of energy was absorbed from the water by the dissolving process. This is why the water cooled down - its thermal energy was transferred to the chemical process.

questions.stem: Thermal decomposition of copper carbonate requires continuous heating: CuCO3 -> CuO + CO2. What happens if the Bunsen burner is turned off before the reaction is complete?

options.text: The reaction speeds up because the products are already hot
The reaction continues to completion because enough energy has been supplied
The reaction stops because endothermic reactions require a continuous energy input
The reaction reverses and copper carbonate re-forms

questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions require a continuous supply of energy to proceed. If the heat source is removed, there is insufficient energy to break the bonds in the remaining copper carbonate, so the decomposition stops. This is a key difference from exothermic reactions, which are self-sustaining once started.

questions.stem: On an energy level diagram for an endothermic reaction, the enthalpy change (Delta H) is shown as +128 kJ/mol. What does the positive sign indicate?

options.text: The reaction releases 128 kJ/mol to the surroundings
The products are at a lower energy level than the reactants
The reaction absorbs 128 kJ/mol from the surroundings; products have more energy than reactants
128 kJ/mol of activation energy is needed

questions.explanation: A positive Delta H value indicates an endothermic reaction. The products have 128 kJ/mol more energy than the reactants. This energy is absorbed from the surroundings. On the energy level diagram, the products line is higher than the reactants line. A negative Delta H would indicate an exothermic reaction.

questions.stem: Sherbet (a sweet) fizzes on the tongue and creates a cooling sensation. It contains citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate. What causes the cooling feeling?

options.text: The fizzing carbon dioxide gas is cold
The citric acid numbs the taste receptors on the tongue
The endothermic reaction between citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate absorbs heat from the tongue
The sugar in the sherbet evaporates and takes heat energy away

questions.explanation: The reaction between citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate is endothermic - it absorbs thermal energy from the surroundings (your tongue). This drop in temperature creates the cooling sensation. The fizzing is from CO2 gas produced, but the cooling effect is due to the endothermic energy change.
